tagline: Across the Perquimans River into Hertford, a former lumber town.
intro: US 17 Business connects Winfall and Hertford across the Perquimans River. North Carolina’s scenic-byway program includes Perquimans Crossing among its Coastal Plain routes. NCDOT describes the program as a way to experience the state’s history, geography and culture.

Hertford thrived on lumber through the early 20th century, using the river to its advantage. Its steel-and-wood floating bridge could be detached from one bank to let boats through, then hauled back into place with lines.

Traveling from Winfall, the business route crosses the river into Hertford, the county seat of Perquimans County. The town’s historic district includes the courthouse and the Church of the Holy Trinity.

moments.title: S Swing Bridge
moments.text: The Perquimans crossing has a history of making room for river traffic. Hertford’s former floating bridge was built of steel and wood. When a boat needed passage, the bridge was released from one bank and floated aside. Afterward, lines pulled the free end back to the bank for reconnection. The later swing bridge had S-shaped approaches.

moments.title: Perquimans County Courthouse
moments.text: Molded brick columns frame the courthouse’s small entrance portico. Built between 1819 and 1825, the Georgian-style brick courthouse has two and a half stories and a four-bay facade. Its T-shaped plan includes rear additions from the late 19th and 20th centuries. The building belongs to the Hertford Historic District and entered the National Register of Historic Places in 1979.

moments.title: Newbold-White House
moments.text: The Newbold-White House has brickwork laid in Flemish bond. Abraham Sanders, a Quaker, purchased the property in 1726 and built the brick house in 1730. His plantation on the Perquimans River produced crops including corn, wheat, flax, indigo and tobacco, as well as wood products. Tree-ring dating places the house’s construction in 1730. The house entered the National Register of Historic Places in 1971.
